data.narrative:
Amber Bio is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Basem Al-Shayeb and Jacob Borrajo that has raised $26M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public Biotech & Health companies (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-sector peers including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Chai Discovery.

Given data constraints, only the stage-progression method is applicable. Using $26M in total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier for the seed-to-next-stage transition yields an implied valuation of $65M. Peer-median triangulation is not viable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds (fewer than 3 datapoints in narrow filters). Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because Amber Bio's revenue is not disclosed; while the Biotech & Health sector shows a 6.6x median P/S multiple across the 3 public tickers, this cannot be applied without the target's revenue figure.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $55M to $75M, centered at $65M. The single-method reliance reflects limited market data for early-stage private biotech. Key uncertainties include Amber Bio's actual revenue or ARR, competitive positioning relative to the named private peers, and technology-risk factors typical in seed-stage life sciences. A wider dataset or direct disclosure of operating metrics would strengthen conviction in this range.
